agency: New York City Department of Sanitation (DSNY)
union: Uniformed Sanitationmen's Association, Local 831, International Brotherhood of Teamsters
title_code_or_exam: Title code 70112; most recent open-competitive exam: No. 2060 (filing June 8-30, 2022; list established Feb. 28, 2024, expires Feb. 28, 2028)

hiring.summary: Sanitation Workers are hired off a ranked civil service list. Candidates pass a computer test and wait to be called in list order, which happens only when DSNY is authorized to hire. Once called they must pass a physical test, background, medical and drug checks, hold a commercial driver license and be 21, then serve an 18-month probation.

nodes.title: Apply when the city opens the exam
nodes.body: The Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) posts a notice of examination and takes online applications. For Exam 2060 the fee was $61 and applicants had to be at least 17½ by the end of the filing period.
nodes.time: Filing window of about three weeks (June 8-30, 2022)
nodes.law: Civil Service Law § 54 (age, as cited in the notice)

nodes.title: Take the multiple-choice test
nodes.body: The test is given at a computer and a score of at least 70% passes. Ten points are added for candidates who qualify for New York City residency credit.

nodes.title: Get ranked on the eligible list
nodes.body: Passing candidates are placed on the list in final score order and given a list number. The Exam 2060 list holds 31,309 names; it was published July 12, 2023, established Feb. 28, 2024 and runs to Feb. 28, 2028.
nodes.time: About 20 months from the close of filing to list establishment for Exam 2060; lists stay active one to four years
nodes.law: Notice of Examination No. 2060; NYC Open Data Civil Service List

nodes.title: Wait to be called for the physical test
nodes.body: Candidates are called in list order, and only when the Department of Sanitation (DSNY) is authorized to hire. The notice warns that not every passing candidate may be called; those called pay a $20 fee.
nodes.time: Varies; DSNY publishes no average wait

nodes.title: Pass document review and background investigation
nodes.body: DSNY's Division of Human Resources interviews candidates, checks proof of age, residency and military service and runs a background investigation. By law the city picks from among the three highest-ranked candidates willing to accept.

nodes.title: Hold a commercial driver license and be 21
nodes.body: By appointment a candidate needs a New York State commercial driver license, Class A or B, with the "N" tank endorsement and no "K" intrastate-only restriction. DSNY offers a one-week course for $1,200, repaid at $30 a paycheck.
nodes.who: Candidate; New York State Department of Motor Vehicles; DSNY

nodes.title: Pass the medical exam and drug tests
nodes.body: DSNY's Medical Division checks that the candidate can perform the job's essential functions. Candidates must pass a drug and alcohol screen plus a federal Department of Transportation drug test, and consent to a federal Clearinghouse query.
nodes.time: Department of Transportation drug test within 30 days before appointment
nodes.law: Federal commercial driver rules, as cited in the notice

nodes.title: Get appointed; meet the residency rule
nodes.body: The candidate is given a date to start training. For the first two years a sanitation worker must live in New York City or in Nassau or Westchester County.
nodes.time: Residency rule applies for the first two years
nodes.law: New York State Public Officers Law, as cited in the notice (section not verified)

nodes.title: Serve an 18-month probation
nodes.body: Probationers must complete a prescribed training course. With the worker's written consent the probation can be extended by up to six months, and it is extended by days spent off the job.
nodes.law: Civil Service Law § 63; Personnel Rules 5.2.1 and 5.2.8

nodes.title: Permanent sanitation worker
nodes.body: After probation the worker holds a permanent competitive-class appointment and can be disciplined only after a hearing under Civil Service Law § 75.

end_to_end.text: For Exam 2060, filing closed June 30, 2022 and the list was established Feb. 28, 2024, about 20 months later. Calls for the physical test then depend on hiring authorization, and DSNY publishes no average wait. Appointment is followed by an 18-month probation, so a candidate who filed in June 2022 could not be a permanent worker before roughly late 2025 at the earliest.

firing.summary: A probationer can be let go by notice, without a hearing. A permanent worker is entitled to written charges, a trial at OATH before an administrative law judge and a final decision by the Sanitation Commissioner, followed by an appeal to the Civil Service Commission or to court. The Local 831 contract's grievance arbitration covers disputes over contract terms; no clause substituting arbitration for the Section 75 process was found in the posted agreement.

nodes.title: An incident or complaint
nodes.body: A supervisor or other source reports alleged misconduct. The Administrative Code lets the sanitation commissioner punish uniformed members for offenses including neglect of duty, rule violations, absence without leave and breach of discipline.
nodes.time: Charges must be brought within 18 months unless the conduct would be a crime

nodes.question: Is the worker still on probation?

nodes.title: Termination by notice, without a hearing
nodes.body: The agency head can end a probationer's employment by notice at the end of probation, after at least two months of service or on failure of the required training course. Section 75 hearing rights cover permanent employees.
nodes.time: Any time after two months of service through the end of probation

nodes.title: Probationer terminated
nodes.body: The DCAS commissioner may, at his or her discretion, restore the person's name to the eligible list if the list still exists.

nodes.title: Possible suspension pending charges
nodes.body: Under the union contract, a local officer cannot summarily suspend a worker alone; the borough officer-in-charge must first try to resolve it with the worker and a union representative. By statute, suspension without pay pending charges is capped at 30 days.
nodes.law: Civil Service Law § 75(3); Local 831 agreement, Art. X

nodes.title: DSNY serves written charges
nodes.body: The worker receives written notice of the charges and has at least eight days to answer in writing. DSNY files the case at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH), and the department bears the burden of proof.
nodes.time: At least 8 days to answer; 8 days (personal service) or 13 days (mail) at OATH

nodes.title: Settlement conference at OATH
nodes.body: An administrative law judge who will not hear the trial conducts a settlement conference. Citywide, 61% of Trials Division cases settled in fiscal 2025.
nodes.who: OATH administrative law judge; DSNY; worker

nodes.title: Trial and report and recommendation
nodes.body: A different judge hears the case and decides it by a preponderance of the evidence. The judge's findings and recommended penalty go to the agency head.
nodes.time: Fiscal 2025 average: 40.73 business days from record closing to decision (all Trials Division cases)

nodes.title: sanitation commissioner decides
nodes.body: The commissioner makes the final decision and may impose a reprimand, a fine up to $100, suspension without pay up to two months, demotion or dismissal. The cause of any fine, suspension or dismissal is recorded in writing.

nodes.title: Appeal to the New York City Civil Service Commission
nodes.body: The appeal must be filed within 20 days of the final decision, with extra time if notice came by mail. The commission's decision is final and cannot be reviewed in court.

nodes.title: Article 78 petition in State Supreme Court
nodes.body: The worker can instead go to court under Article 78 of the Civil Practice Law and Rules. The petition must be filed within four months after the decision becomes final.

stats.text: The active Exam 2060 sanitation worker list has 31,309 names (New York City Open Data, accessed Sept. 11, 2026). The dataset does not show how many have been appointed or passed over.
The Exam 2060 list was published July 12, 2023 and established Feb. 28, 2024; it expires Feb. 28, 2028. No newer sanitation worker exam appears on DCAS's exam schedule through June 30, 2027.

In fiscal 2025 the OATH Trials Division took an average of 40.73 business days to issue a decision after the record closed (35.96 in fiscal 2024), and 79% of decisions came within 45 business days. These figures cover all Trials Division cases, not only Sanitation cases.

The OATH Trials Division case dataset lists 33 Section 75 cases with 'Sanitation' in the case name, opened 2017-2025. Judges recommended termination in 19, suspension in 11 and dismissal of charges in 3; the median was 156 days from opening to report. This subset is a name match and may not be every DSNY case.

caveats: Exam 2060 (2022) is the most recent Sanitation Worker exam found; the fee, dates and conditions described are from its amended notice and may change for the next exam.

The residency rule on DSNY's careers page (New York City, Nassau or Westchester) matches only the first two years in the exam notice; after two years the notice also allows Suffolk, Orange, Rockland and Putnam counties.

The Local 831 unit agreement on the Office of Labor Relations site is the 2007-2011 contract; the 2022-2028 economic agreement says earlier unit terms continue unless modified. Both are scanned PDFs, so quotes come from OCR text and could contain small transcription errors.

Administrative Code § 16-106 caps Sanitation Department suspensions and pay forfeitures at 30 days, while Civil Service Law § 75(3) allows suspension without pay of up to two months after a hearing. Civil Service Law § 76(4) keeps local laws in force; how the two interact in DSNY penalties was not verified.
OATH's 45-business-day figure is a Mayor's Management Report performance measure, not a rule deadline. No rule requiring the Sanitation Commissioner to decide within a set number of days was found.
Curly quotation marks in source PDFs were changed to straight quotes; ellipses mark omitted text within quotes.
Civil Service Law § 75 and § 76 quotes were taken through a web-fetch tool that returned excerpts, not the raw statute page; the § 75(3) suspension sentence comes from the public.law mirror.

The Administrative Code and Charter text came from American Legal Publishing's database through the BetaNYC nyc-charter tool and the readthedocs mirror, because codelibrary.amlegal.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches.
unverified: Physical test content: the exam notice says a description would be released later. No official DCAS description was found, only test-prep sites, so the events and weights are left out.
Length and content of DSNY's training academy for new hires: the notice requires a prescribed training course but gives no duration, and no official DSNY page stating one was found.

Role of the DSNY Department Advocate / Office of Employment and Disciplinary Matters in drafting charges and negotiating with the union: this appears only in a search snippet of a cityjobs.nyc.gov posting, and the site refused connections.
DSNY Code of Conduct and internal disciplinary procedures: not located on nyc.gov.
Department of Investigation involvement in DSNY discipline: no official document fetched describes it.

Average time from list establishment to appointment, and the number appointed from the Exam 2060 list: no official figure found. The DCAS list-announcement document on the Government Publications Portal returned 403.
Whether the one-in-three selection rule under Civil Service Law § 61 is used in practice for Sanitation Worker: DSNY says it calls candidates in list-number order.
Exact wording of the crime exception in Civil Service Law § 75(4): only a fragment was retrieved.
Which section of the Public Officers Law sets the Sanitation Worker residency rule: the exam notice cites the law without naming a section.
Court doctrine that probationers can be dismissed without a hearing absent bad faith: no decision was fetched, so the chart relies on Personnel Rule 5.2.7 and the text of Civil Service Law § 75(1).
Whether a full successor unit agreement after 2011 changed Article X (grievances): none is posted on the Office of Labor Relations uniformed contracts page.
